summary.headline: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend a preliminary $70.9 million FY27 operating budget while refining guidance for the March 2 Special Town Meeting.
summary.summary: The Advisory Committee reviewed the updated FY27 town budget model, which currently projects an estimated 5.3 percent average single-family tax increase without an override, though members warned future years will face severe fiscal pressures. The committee met with Public Works and Recreation leadership to discuss capital vehicle deferrals and a planned $1.1 million CPC park project. Members also reviewed the Police Department budget, which includes two previously approved officer positions, and formally voted to recommend a preliminary $70,887,098 operating budget. Finally, the committee reviewed and edited draft advisory recommendations on four school building and roof articles heading to the March 2 Special Town Meeting.

topics.title: FY27 budget model and multi-year financial forecast
topics.summary: The committee examined the updated FY27 operating budget model and preliminary out-year forecasts through FY30. Under current assumptions, single-family taxes are estimated to rise about 5.3 percent, with hopes that Algonquin regional school assessment increases drop from 7 percent to 5 percent. Members stressed that while FY27 can balance just under the levy limit with roughly $91,000 to spare, significant debt service and slowing revenue growth will likely push the town into override territory in FY28 and beyond.
key_details: Current model shows a 5.3 percent year-over-year tax increase for an average single-family home.
FY27 remains within the levy limit with approximately $91,000 in excess levy capacity.
Short-term borrowing interest is about $300,000 in FY27 but jumps to $1.6 million in FY28.
The town benefited from an additional $1 million in certified free cash this year that cannot be counted on next year.
Committee members noted that contractually obligated salary increases and employee benefits drive a 3 percent to 5 percent baseline expense growth.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; multi-year numbers will be presented to Town Meeting for context.
topics.why_it_matters: Determines local property tax rates and signals whether Southborough will require operational budget overrides in the next one to two fiscal years.

topics.title: DPW capital requests and equipment deferrals
topics.summary: Public Works representative Bill Cundiff met with the committee to discuss proposed capital vehicle purchases. Cundiff explained that front-line snow and ice equipment, including a $235,000 cab and chassis replacement, is experiencing costly frequent breakdowns and should not be delayed. However, he agreed that a $52,475 ground service dump truck could potentially be postponed for one year if budget reductions are necessary.
key_details: A cab and chassis replacement is budgeted at $235,000, reusing the body from the existing truck.
A ground service dump truck is requested at $52,475, which could be deferred for one year.
DPW maintains six to eight large front-line dump trucks that have a 10 to 12 year useful life.
A previously proposed tree inventory survey article was pulled and deferred to seek grant funding.
topics.outcome: The committee noted the potential deferral of the $52,475 dump truck for further capital budget deliberations.

topics.title: Fayville Park improvement project update
topics.summary: Recreation Director Travis Matteson updated the committee on the proposed Fayville Memorial Park project. The project, estimated at roughly $1.1 million, has been deferred to the fall Town Meeting to allow consideration by the Community Preservation Committee and to await word on a federal Land and Water Conservation Fund grant. The design includes repurposing an underutilized tee-ball field into a small dog park, an accessible walking path, and a 2,000-square-foot recirculating splash pad.
key_details: Total project cost is estimated at approximately $1.1 million, with $700,000 to $800,000 for the splash pad.
The project will be funded through Community Preservation Act funds and potential grants, not general capital borrowing.
The splash pad will use recirculated, treated water to limit water usage and mitigate drought concerns.
Annual operational water costs are estimated at $4,000 to $5,000, intended to be covered by recreation program fees.
topics.outcome: Information only; the article is slated for the fall 2026 Special Town Meeting.

topics.title: Police Department budget and staffing review
topics.summary: Member Howard Rose presented an update from his budget liaison meeting with Police Chief Ryan Newell. The department's operating expenses are flat, but salary lines are increasing due to the newly negotiated collective bargaining agreement and full-year funding for two additional patrol officers authorized at last year's Town Meeting. The chief reported strong department morale, 40 applicants for open positions, and noted that increased traffic enforcement has generated over $100,000 in additional town revenue.
key_details: Police operating expenses are held flat year-over-year, with increases driven by contractual raises and staffing.
The department received 40 applicants for open positions, which include two positions funded starting in April and a replacement for a vacant midnight shift.
The department is transitioning from larger patrol SUVs to smaller Ford Broncos with 1.3-liter engines to save purchase and fuel costs.
Traffic enforcement and citations produced an increase of over $100,000 in local revenue between FY24 and FY25.
topics.outcome: The committee concurred with maintaining the police staffing and operating budget as submitted.

topics.title: Preliminary recommendation of FY27 operating budget
topics.summary: The committee discussed whether to formally endorse the operational budget lines ahead of the Select Board's upcoming meeting. Members agreed that municipal department heads had held operational costs to level service, leaving capital articles and bond authorizations as the primary remaining variables to adjust. The committee voted unanimously to recommend a preliminary operating budget figure of $70,887,098 to Town Meeting.
key_details: The motion covers only the operational budget lines, excluding capital debt articles.
Operating budgets within town control are largely finalized, though regional school assessments could still see minor adjustments.
Facilities recently submitted an unexpected request for a $65,000 replacement utility van that the committee will evaluate under capital articles.
topics.outcome: Passed 6-0 to recommend a preliminary FY27 operating budget of $70,887,098.
topics.why_it_matters: Sets the Advisory Committee's baseline recommendation for Southborough town government and school operations for Town Meeting.

topics.title: Advisory report and recommendations for March 2 Special Town Meeting
topics.summary: The committee reviewed draft text and rationale for the Advisory Committee Report to be published for the March 2, 2026 Special Town Meeting. Members focused on Articles 1, 2, and 3, which propose feasibility studies for elementary school renovations or consolidation, and Article 4, which requests funding for the Neary Elementary School roof. The committee discussed framing Article 1 as the fiscally responsible, baseline option to evaluate renovating Neary while preserving the option to utilize a new roof, whereas Articles 2 and 3 involve higher study costs and exploring alternative school closures.
key_details: The committee previously voted 7-0 to support Article 1 ($175,000 for a Neary renovation study) and 7-0 for Article 4 (Neary roof replacement).
The committee voted 3-4 against supporting Article 2 ($500,000 for a multi-school study) and 3-4 against Article 3 ($324,000 for a Finn School study).
Members emphasized in the draft that approving the Neary roof makes a Neary renovation study the most practical path to protect the roof investment.
The draft letter will clarify that voting yes on Articles 2 or 3 would create potential budget pressure that could require an override or capital cuts.
topics.outcome: The chair will compile feedback and circulate a final draft report by Monday for member sign-off.
topics.why_it_matters: Provides voters with the town finance committee's formal evaluations and cost trade-offs on multi-million dollar school facility choices.

topics.title: Meeting schedule and Special Town Meeting logistics
topics.summary: Members discussed meeting plans leading up to the Special Town Meeting on Monday, March 2, 2026. The committee determined that an on-site meeting immediately prior to Town Meeting at Trottier Middle School is unnecessary unless unexpected amendments or motions arise on the floor. The committee will review the draft report early in the coming week and call a mid-week meeting only if substantive disagreements emerge.
key_details: Special Town Meeting takes place Monday, March 2, 2026.
The chair will circulate the draft advisory booklet letter by Monday, February 23.
Members will review by Tuesday to determine if an additional meeting is required.
topics.outcome: No pre-Town Meeting session scheduled; members will coordinate report edits via email.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee noted that all outstanding minutes through October 14 had been approved at their prior meeting. Member Claire Reynolds mentioned she was testing artificial intelligence tools for summarizing committee meeting notes. The chair opened the floor for public comment, but none was offered, and the committee voted to adjourn.
key_details: No meeting minutes required approval.
No members of the public offered comments.
topics.outcome: The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:35 PM by unanimous roll call vote.

votes.motion: Recommend to Town Meeting and the Select Board a preliminary FY27 operating budget of $70,887,098.
